title: A Relationship Between Nonphysical Quasi-probabilities and Nonlocality Objectivity

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: For a semi-trivial perp state, β is said to have only one nonzero row or column vector. If β is a 3×3 matrix with one nonzero row/column vector v, then β^T β is a rank-one 3×3 matrix whose only nonzero eigenvalue is ||v||^2. It is not a 3×1 vector of squared components, as written in Eq. (8). For example, a single nonzero row (β1,β2,β3) gives β^T β with entries β_iβ_j, not diag(β1^2,β2^2,β3^2).

predicted_errors.error_location: Eq. (9) and the subsequent claim that the intersection is nonempty
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: For a rank-one β with vector entries (β1,β2,β3), the eigenvalues of β^T β are {||β||^2,0,0}, so the Horodecki parameter M is ||β||^2, not a sum of the two largest squared components. Thus the conditions β1^2+β2^2+β3^2>1 and β1^2+β2^2≤1 cannot jointly be the nonlocality condition, and cannot be satisfied with a rank-one β since M>1 would require the total norm >1 while the first two components satisfy ≤1. The claimed SIN region is therefore not a valid eigenvalue region for the states under discussion.

predicted_errors.error_location: Definition 1.3 and Theorem 1.4; also the discussion after Eq. (8)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Qubit swapping replaces the correlation matrix β by β^T. Since β^T β and β β^T have the same spectra, M is invariant under qubit swapping. Therefore a Hermitian trace-one operator cannot be nonlocal with M>1 but have its qubit-swapped version be local with M≤1. The proposed swap-intolerant nonlocality is impossible under the Horodecki criterion itself.

From Eq. (7), positive semidefiniteness requires |E−C| ≤ r_- (for the second eigenvalue family) and |E+C| ≤ r_+ (for the first family). Therefore E must lie in the sphere (C,r_-) and −E in (C,r_+). Proposition 2.1 states the opposite: E in (C,r_+) and −E in (C,r_-).

The text attributes the experimentally testable Bell inequality to 1966. The standard experimentally convenient Bell-CHSH inequality is due to Clauser, Horne, Shimony and Holt in 1969. Bell's 1966 paper was not the source of the CHSH-style experimentally testable inequality, so the citation/date is likely misattributed.
